newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower on moderate volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower on moderate volumes.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended lower Wednesday on moderate volumes, with most CRB-index commodities down as funds took profits on seasonal rallies, analysts said.

"Precious metals have been a little bearish in recent days, after news of the Swiss plan to sell some gold, but Swiss National Bank chairman Meyer today again said no gold would be sold until 1999," said Jeff Kowal, a fund manager with Toronto-based Friedberg Mercantile Group.
"But overall commodities were down across the board today, and that may have rubbed off on precious metals also."

Last week the Swiss government announced a plan to set up a fund to compensate Holocaust victims, financed by selling some Swiss gold reserves, though the plan requires a change to the Swiss constitution.
COMEX April gold ended down $1.90 at $353.50 an ounce, after trading a $355.40-351.90 range. Estimated total COMEX gold futures volume was 33,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $351.80/30, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $351.40 and the New York close Tuesday at $353.30/80.

Implied gold lease rates fell to their lowest levels in several months Wednesday around 1.07 percent for one month, suggesting there was little speculative shorting of bullion resuming yet, analysts said.

"But any signs that prices are running out of steam should bring short selling into the market, although there seems to be reasonably strong interim support at $350," CPM Group New York analyst Ted Kempf said.
Producer hedging has been noted in recent days though, after gold prices recovered in the past month from three year lows around $336.00 in February.
Australian miner Equigold said Wednesday it had placed forward gold sales covering the first 40,000 ounces of its share of production from the Dalgaranga mine in western Australia.
The hedge program would result in the company achieving a flat forward price of A$542.00 an ounce through to the end of 1998, the company said.
The price of gold in Australian dollars is currently around $442.00 an ounce after falling to fresh five year lows this week as the Australian dollar strengthened.
COMEX May silver ended down 5.7 cents at $5.230, after trading a $5.305-5.210 range.
"In what appears to be a broadening top (chart) formation silver continues to lose momentum around $5.25 in the May contract," CRB analyst Terry Roggensack said.
"The sharp decline in open interest highlights a large number of small speculator longs giving up on the recent breakout.

Open interest in COMEX silver fell a further 1,183 lots Wednesday to 89,019 contracts, down from a high of 100,688 lots on February 20, when nearby-active month silver broke out of a year-long downtrend.
NYMEX April platinum closed down $2.50 at $384.50 an ounce, after trading a $389.50-382.50 range.
NYMEX June palladium close down $6.85 at $154.25 an ounce, after seeing a contract high at $161.25 Tuesday.
Reports suggesting Russian palladium supplies to Japan may resume before the end of March undermined platinum group metals prices, traders said.
But an official at the U.S. branch of Russia's metal export agency, Almaz, told Reuters Wednesday he was unable to confirm reports of a resumption of palladium supplies.

Last month an Almaz official in Tokyo said there would be no Russian supplies of palladium to Japan in March and supplies were unlikely in April also. He also said Russian expected to ship less palladium this year.
Russia accounts for about 60 percent of world supplies of palladium with most coming from the Norilsk plant and Russian stockpiles.
